editorial:
You meet Mateo as he tries to keep life together while his best friend turns every night into a messy drinking session. The movie plays the chaos for laughs, but it also shows how exhausting it is to love someone who keeps choosing the bottle. Their friendship feels real, loud, and messy, with jokes landing between awkward silences and bad decisions. It is a comedy first, yet the alcoholism angle gives the story a sharper edge than a simple party movie.

The acting carries the film, especially the way Mateo shifts from patient to fed up without losing warmth. The pacing stays quick, with scenes moving from bars to morning-after regrets before you get bored. Some jokes repeat and the ending wraps up a little too neatly, but the heart keeps it watchable. If you enjoy character-driven comedies with a little bite, this is a solid pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Mateo finally stops covering for his friend and walks away from another drunken disaster. His friend hits rock bottom, gets help, and shows up sober to apologize. Mateo accepts the apology but sets clear boundaries, so their friendship continues on healthier terms. The twist is that the friend’s worst night was partly staged to force Mateo to stop enabling him.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves buddy comedies with emotional honesty.
